category: EP Purpose and the ECM Duel
tags: ep purpose and the ecm duel
prompt: Per PAM 3-0702-01, EP safeguards personnel, facilities and equipment from the effects of what?
options: Emissions in the spectrum, whether friendly, adversary or natural
Adversary jamming of the unit's radio net, and nothing from friendly or natural sources
Enemy direction finding and intercept only
Emissions of the unit's own jammers only
explanation: Slide 7: EP safeguards from the effects of spectrum emissions, including friendly, adversary or natural electromagnetic interference.

category: EP Purpose and the ECM Duel
tags: ep purpose and the ecm duel
prompt: In the ECM versus ECCM duel, the enemy spot-jams our channel and our radios begin to hop. What does the enemy do next?
options: Withdraws the jammer to the rear
Switches to barrage jamming
Switches to direction finding
Begins spoofing the GPS position
explanation: Slide 6: the enemy spot-jams, our radios hop, the enemy switches to barrage, and we lower power, mask with terrain and switch to PACE.

category: EP Purpose and the ECM Duel
tags: ep purpose and the ecm duel
prompt: Which event does the news slide place in February 2024 in the West Philippine Sea?
options: Pilots losing GPS on approach and CAAP requiring interference reports
A GPS spoofing incident on a naval patrol
Command posts and drone teams found by their emissions and then hit by fires in the field
Increased jamming affecting ships' and land-based communications, mostly cellphones
explanation: Slide 5: PN reported increased jamming that affected ships' and land-based comms, mostly cellphones; the others are the airport and Ukraine items.

prompt: Sending a situation report at the same minute every hour breaks which radio-discipline rule?
options: Transmit only when needed
Smart antenna placement
Short transmissions
Vary your routine
explanation: Slide 9: vary your routine - no fixed report times or patterns.

prompt: Which group of measures answers the enemy question 'Can I READ you?'
options: Hardening, spectrum management and PACE alternate means
Emission control, low power and terrain masking
Frequency hopping, directional antennas and PACE alternate means
Encryption (secure mode), brevity codes, and saying less, less often
explanation: Slide 8: FIND is answered by EMCON, low power and masking; JAM by hopping, directional antennas and PACE; READ by encryption, brevity codes and saying less.

prompt: Camouflage nets block stray radiation from a directional antenna when they are placed:
options: On the sides and back of the antenna
On top of the antenna only
Over the front of the antenna
Between the antenna and the friendly station
explanation: Slide 10: camouflage nets on the sides and back of directional antennas block stray radiation.

prompt: Which approach best masks a unit's emissions in an area with busy commercial networks, according to the lesson?
options: Transmit at high power to rise above the civilian traffic
Use the spectrum as nearby users do and avoid predictable report times
Use unusual frequencies so military signals are easy to separate
Send reports at fixed times to keep the pattern stable
explanation: Slides 11 and 23: busy commercial networks near Kyiv helped mask military signals; avoid predictable report times and patterns.

prompt: In the Ukraine lessons, command posts were high-payoff targets because their emissions were:
options: Stationary and constant
Unencrypted and loud
Sent on a single channel
Broadcast at high power
explanation: Slide 23: command posts were high-payoff targets because their emissions were stationary and constant.

prompt: Which EMCON level applies once an attack has occurred, with non-essential emitters off and alternates in use?
options: EMCON 4, RED
EMCON 3, AMBER
EMCON 2, YELLOW
EMCON 5, BLACK
explanation: Slide 12: EMCON 4, RED - an attack has occurred; non-essential emitters are off and alternates are used.

prompt: What is the posture at EMCON 2, YELLOW?
options: Operate normally with encryption on
Limit transmissions and watch power levels
Encrypt, hop and use directional antennas, with unencrypted systems off
Switch non-essential emitters off and use alternates
explanation: Slide 12: EMCON 2, YELLOW applies at a risk of attack - limit transmissions and watch power levels.

prompt: What is required of unencrypted systems at EMCON 3, AMBER?
options: They are turned off
They continue to operate using brevity codes
They are isolated as compromised systems
They are limited to short transmissions at low power
explanation: Slide 12: at EMCON 3, AMBER, the unit encrypts, hops and uses directional antennas, and unencrypted systems are off.

prompt: Encryption alone does not stop jamming because it protects:
options: Where the transmitter is, not what is said
Who is speaking, not what is said
What is said, not whether the signal gets through
When the station transmits, not what is said
explanation: Slides 14 and 25: encryption protects WHAT you say; anti-jam protects WHETHER it gets through.

prompt: Which of the following describes spread spectrum?
options: The radar changes frequency from one pulse to the next
The radio jumps channels many times per second in a pattern only friendly radios know
The signal is spread so that it is harder to detect and jam
A long, coded pulse is squeezed on receive for range detail
explanation: Slide 13: spread spectrum spreads the signal so it is harder to detect and jam; hopping is the channel-jumping technique.

prompt: PA tactical radios (Harris, Combat Net Radio System) are required to have which two features?
options: Spread spectrum and directional antennas
Frequency agility and hardening
Encryption and CRPA antennas
Frequency hopping and encryption
explanation: Slide 13: PA tactical radios are required to have hopping and encryption; use them in hop mode.

prompt: In the quick test, the noise stays after the antenna is disconnected. What should be suspected?
options: Friendly interference from other units
Enemy jamming from outside
Your own radio, cables or power
Terrain and distance
explanation: Slide 15: if the noise drops, it comes from outside; if the noise stays, suspect your own radio, cables or power.

prompt: Which of the following is a sign of jamming listed on the recognize slide?
options: Voice is received clearly while data fails
The GPS position moves smoothly with the vehicle
Squelch opens with no one talking
Only one station drops while every other stays clear
explanation: Slide 15: signs include steady noise, squelch opening with no one talking, broken voice, every station dropping at once and a wrong GPS position.

prompt: Which step follows 'keep operating' in the reaction sequence for suspected jamming?
options: Report: tell higher headquarters by an alternate means if needed, at once
Announce: tell the net that jamming is present
Adjust: raise power briefly or move behind cover
Check equipment: antenna, cables, battery, settings and fills
explanation: Slide 16: step 1 keep operating, step 2 check equipment, step 3 adjust, step 4 report.

prompt: A section's primary hop-and-secure radio net is jammed, and it has a written PACE plan. What should it do?
options: Wait for higher headquarters to name the contingency
Move to the alternate at the agreed trigger, as rehearsed
Go directly to the emergency means
Raise power on the primary until the jamming stops
explanation: Slide 18: rehearse the switch and know the trigger; the alternate follows the primary.

prompt: Which GPS protection measure nulls out jammers?
options: CRPA antennas
Brevity codes
Map and compass cross-checks
Terrain masking
explanation: Slide 19: CRPA antennas null out jammers; the map and compass check detects spoofing.

prompt: Two radios sited together on the same frequencies interfere with each other. Which measure from the lesson addresses this?
options: Switch both radios to clear voice
Move both antennas to the hilltop for wider coverage and a clearer signal
Separate the antennas and use only the frequencies assigned by the S6
Raise the power on both radios until the interference stops
explanation: Slide 20: for compatibility, separate antennas, do not co-site on the same frequencies and use only assigned frequencies from the S6.

prompt: Which checks confirm hardening every time equipment is set up?
options: Antenna height, azimuth and EMCON level
Cable shielding, connectors and grounding
Fills, frequencies and the PACE plan
Battery level, squelch and call signs
explanation: Slide 20: check cable shielding, connectors and grounding on every setup.

prompt: A long, coded pulse is squeezed on receive for range detail and anti-jam margin. Which sensor ECCM technique is this?
options: Low-probability-of-intercept
Pulse compression
Frequency agility
Sidelobe blanking
explanation: Slide 21: pulse compression squeezes a long, coded pulse on receive for range detail and anti-jam margin.
